decisions.reason: The client requires existing missing no-referral commissions to be reflected so twelve primary mints account for twelve commissions, and explicitly applies this visibility to NFT attributes as well as the leaderboard.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, we have completed 12 mints, so that should amount to 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**Even if no referral code is used, a ticket and commission are still issued**.

Currently, **when a code is used**, it is accurately reflected on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

If **no referral code is used**, the ticket and commission are assigned at random.
(B**ut they must still be reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I believe that since your most recent fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 2 mints have been reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
However, the missing tickets have not been backfilled.

The commissions from these purchases without a code are also still not reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot, you will see that I have an NFT showing 2 tickets but only 1 x $5 commission. That should not be possible because each ticket includes a $5 commission.

Also, in my leaderboard screenshot, only 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions are accounted for out of 12 total mints.
Whether or not a referral code is used, 12 mints should result in 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions.

decisions.reason: The client requires previously missing ticket and commission values to be reflected in NFT attributes, making historical attribute backfill necessary.

decisions.reason: Ticket and commission accounting does not change NFT image sizing, image rendering, or media behavior.
The reference to twelve completed mints supplies accounting context but does not change the rule governing which owned NFTs appear in the dashboard.
Randomly allocated rewards from no-referral mints do not establish a change to how referral counts are displayed.
The source changes ticket and commission reconciliation, not public referral-count statistics.
The source does not change the countdown label, its sales-based measure, or the draw trigger.
The source does not establish or change any prize-pool balance or public prize-pool display rule.
Twelve completed mints is contextual evidence for reward reconciliation, not a change to the public mint counter's counting basis.
The current FAQ state already states that no-referral mints allocate commissions and tickets randomly, and the source does not request a FAQ content revision.
Reward allocation and visibility for no-referral mints does not alter fiat-buyer wallet creation, custody, access, or provisioning behavior.
Historical reward-accounting backfill does not change the approved replacement-contract migration or legacy-state policy.
